1.d: Own a home of your own with no mortgage
1.s: You paid the whole price in one go, and the agent stared at your transfer record for three solid seconds. The deed is in your hands with a single name on it — yours. One of the rarest achievements on this planet.

2.d: Passive income covers your living costs
2.s: No more worrying about bills, no more forcing yourself to work on days you cannot stand it. You finally own the most expensive thing on Earth: freedom. And you learned that it was never the money that made you happy — it was the choices money buys.

3.d: Own several generations of game consoles
3.s: Your shelf holds one generation after another: Switch, PS5, Xbox, and the classics long out of production. Each one carries the memories of a different era. You were never collecting machines — you were collecting pieces of your youth.

4.d: Leave footprints on every continent on Earth
4.s: You left footprints on all seven continents. From Antarctic ice to African savanna, from old European towns to South American rainforest — you measured this planet with your own feet. It is more beautiful, more fragile and more worth protecting than you imagined.

5.d: Get up early every day for 365 days straight
5.s: One of the hardest achievements on Earth. Every morning you fought the gravity of the bed, the pull of the phone and the weight of exhaustion. But those early hours, those quiet mornings, became the most valuable thing you own. You have outplayed 99% of the players.

6.d: 42.195 km, measured with your own two feet
6.s: At kilometre 35 you nearly quit — legs like lead, lungs in a vise. But you turned the final corner, saw the finish line and spent everything you had. By the time the medal touched your neck, you were already thinking about the next marathon.

7.d: No mortgage, no car loan, no consumer debt
7.s: In an age where everyone owes someone, you owe no one. No mortgage pressure, no credit card dread — you live lighter than most people do. Not because you earn more, but because you know how to control your desires.

8.d: Master a language other than your mother tongue
8.s: From the alphabet to fluent conversation took years. That language opened a window onto scenery you had never seen and people you would never have met. The world got bigger because of it.

9.d: Spend a night camping out in the wild
9.s: The campfire crackled, the stars were within reach, insects and wind carried from far away. No city light pollution out here. Lying in your sleeping bag you saw the Milky Way in full for the first time — the night sky is this beautiful.

10.d: Beat gravity with nothing but discipline
10.s: You gave up late-night snacks, went to the gym daily and doubted your life in front of the scale. Then one day you put on that old pair of jeans and the zipper slid up without a fight. In that moment you felt capable of anything.

11.d: Take a trip to a foreign country
11.s: The first entry stamp lands in your passport. You stand on a foreign street where the air smells unfamiliar and the signs make no sense, and you are thrilled. The world is larger and stranger than you imagined, and you have just taken the first step.

12.d: Cross a thousand miles just to see one person
12.s: You bought a plane or train ticket and crossed half the country just to see that one person. Maybe you only shared a meal or took a short walk. But a heart that travelled a thousand miles is worth more than anything.

13.d: Witness the sky's own light show near the Arctic Circle
13.s: You waited three hours in minus twenty degrees. When the green curtain began to dance overhead you forgot the cold. It was the most beautiful light you have ever seen — belonging to no city, only to the planet itself.

14.d: Have a friend of ten years or more you trust without condition
14.s: Ten years. You have seen each other at your worst, traded your deepest secrets, argued and made up. In a world of people constantly coming and going, one person is always still there — that is worth more than anything.

15.d: Keep a hobby going for five years without quitting
15.s: Five years of drawing, running, writing, photography or piano. The people around you changed again and again; this one small thing you kept. It may bring no fame and no money, but it gives your soul somewhere to rest.

16.d: Know exactly where every cent goes
16.s: You tracked every purchase for a year — and found out how much of it went on milk tea. You started to rethink what is actually worth buying. That is not stinginess; it is respect for your own labour.

17.d: Build an organisation of your own
17.s: You quit the stable job and registered a company with your savings. For three months there was no income, only anxiety. Then the first order landed — and you looked at that number and cried.

18.d: Stay awake for more than 24 hours
18.s: You watched the clock tick past the 24-hour mark. Eyelids heavy, mind slow, and still you could not sleep. Maybe stress, maybe excitement, maybe plain insomnia. Either way, you are testing the limits of human physiology.

19.d: Reach somewhere more than six time zones from home
19.s: You flew for over ten hours. Your body insists it is three in the morning; outside the window it is blazing noon. Standing on a foreign street it hits you: the world is much bigger than you thought.

20.d: Speak two or more regional dialects fluently
20.s: You do not just speak the standard language — you can switch into two or more dialects and blend right in. Every dialect is a local cultural cipher, and you hold several of the keys.

21.d: Study more than ten hours outside class in a single day
21.s: At two in the morning you were still grinding through problems and your roommate said you had lost it. You did not know what you were fighting for — only that you refused to lose to people who worked harder. Years later those desperate days are the purest time of your life.

22.s: You wrote the date on the last page of the fiftieth book and remembered stumbling through the first one. These books did not change your fate, but they changed how you see the world — and that is enough.

23.d: Sleep ten hours or more in a single day
23.s: One rare day off, you turned off every alarm and slept for over ten hours. You woke to good sunlight, a growling stomach and a completely empty head. Doing nothing at all has never felt so luxurious.

24.d: Prove that discipline is more than motivational talk
24.s: Day one you were full of fire. Day ten you wanted to quit. Day thirty it felt routine. On the morning of day one hundred you opened your eyes and realised the thing that once took willpower had become part of your life.

25.d: Decide on a whim and leave right away
25.s: On Friday night you had a sudden idea and bought a ticket. On Saturday morning you were drinking coffee on a street in another city. No plan, no companion — just a backpack and a heart pointed somewhere far away. The best gift you ever gave yourself.

26.d: Save a stranger's life with 400 ml of blood
26.s: You rolled up your sleeve and watched the needle enter the vein. The nurse said your blood might save someone on an operating table. It struck you then: anyone can be somebody's hero — no superpowers needed, just a little courage.

27.d: Complete a handmade project entirely on your own
27.s: From nothing — a block of wood, a length of thread, a lump of clay — something whole took shape in your hands. Imperfect, but one of a kind. The joy of making things is in the making, not in how polished the result looks.

28.d: Become an expert in a very narrow field
28.s: Five years, maybe more, and finally the word Doctor appears on that thin certificate. You stand at the summit of academia looking out over the edge of human knowledge — and discover there is an even bigger unknown beyond it.

29.d: Log more than 1000 hours in a single game
29.s: The counter says you have put over a thousand hours into this one game. People ask whether it was worth it and you do not know how to answer. Those late nights, those teammates, that laughter and those tears — no number can measure them.

30.d: Watch more than thirty films in one year
30.s: Your watchlist keeps growing and your log is dense. Every film is a window onto a different life. Thirty, fifty, a hundred — your view of the world shifted quietly in all that light and shadow.

31.d: Build the living space you always wanted, by hand
31.s: You painted walls, hung lights and assembled furniture, turning a bare shell into the home you dreamed of. Every detail carries your effort, and your friends' gasps when they visited were the best reward of all.

32.d: Say what words cannot, with music
32.s: You played a piece all the way through for the first time. Fingering still clumsy, timing still rough — but the melody came out of your own hands. Now you understand why people say music is the language of the soul.

33.d: Stop relying on money from your family
33.s: The first time you paid rent, bought groceries and covered the utility bills with money you earned, it stung a little — and you felt prouder than ever. From today you are an adult who stands on their own.

34.d: Become the organiser at the centre of family gatherings
34.s: You arranged the whole family dinner: booked the restaurant, set the seating, ordered the dishes, remembered everyone's tastes. Looking at all those smiling faces you realised you have become the backbone of this family.

35.d: Keep three or fewer truly close friends
35.s: Your contacts list is long but your real friends number two or three. You do not chase socialising and you do not feel lonely. Quality over quantity, always — a few true friends beat a thousand casual likes.

36.d: Overcome fear and move people with your voice
36.s: You stood on stage with shaking legs and a trembling voice. Then you finished and the room applauded — and you found that being afraid was never as terrible as the fear itself.

37.d: Keep a cat or dog for more than five years
37.s: Five years, and they have gone from a tiny kitten or pup to the most important part of your life. They wait when you are out; they fly at you when you come home. They cannot speak, but the love they give is purer than anyone's.

38.d: Run into your own people far from home
38.s: You heard your own language on a foreign street and were flooded with familiarity. You talked for a long time, swapped contacts, then went your separate ways. But you will never forget that afternoon's coffee.

39.d: Unlock the skill of speaking to another culture
39.s: Years of memorising words and drilling pronunciation, and then one day you told a joke in another language — and the other person laughed. In that moment you knew you truly owned the language.

40.d: Own a permanent coordinate on this planet
40.s: You signed your name on the purchase contract, taking on twenty years of commitment in a single stroke. But when you turned the key in the door of your new home, you knew it was worth it.

41.d: Scroll for eight hours without leaving the screen
41.s: You only meant to relax for five minutes, and then you looked up and it was dark. Battery down from 80% to 5%, neck aching, thumb still moving. The algorithm knows you better than you know yourself — that is the frightening part.

42.d: Keep a houseplant alive for a whole year
42.s: You watered, fertilised and moved it into the sun — and it actually survived a whole year. You proudly posted a photo: not a plant killer any more. That is when you learned that keeping something alive takes more patience than you thought.

43.s: You walked off the plane into unfamiliar smells and signs you could not read, buzzing with excitement. The world really is enormous — big enough that a whole lifetime would not cover it.

44.d: Cry over more than ten films or shows
44.s: You are not a crier, but some films simply will not let your eyes stay dry. The tenth time you wiped your face in a cinema you accepted it: sensitivity is not weakness, it is proof of how deeply you can feel.

45.d: Take a road trip behind the wheel
45.s: Hands on the wheel, friends or your partner beside you, heading south along the coast. Music up, windows down, wind pouring in, all of you singing loudly. There is no destination on this road — the scenery along the way is the point.

46.s: The first time you said no, you were anxious, certain the world would collapse. Nothing happened. Instead you felt lighter than you had in years. Saying no is a skill too.

47.d: Average under seven hours of sleep a day
47.s: Six hours has become normal and caffeine is your daily shield. You tell yourself it is the price of ambition, but you also know your body will come collecting one day.

48.d: Stay single for four years or more as an adult
48.s: Your friends paired off, married, had kids — and you are still single. Sometimes it makes you anxious, but more often you think freedom is wonderful. Love cannot be rushed and cannot be forced.

49.d: Treat your family to an expensive meal with your own money
49.s: You booked the restaurant you had always wanted to take them to but never dared to pay for. Watching your parents' faces — half pained by the price, half bursting with pride — you knew it was worth it. Not because the food was good, but because you could finally repay them.

50.s: You walked the campus again and again in your gown, trying to memorise every path. Four years for a single sheet of paper — but you know the story behind that paper is the real fortune.

51.s: Night after night you finished season after season, agonising over the characters and gasping at the twists. Ten shows, hundreds of hours, lived inside one parallel world after another. Binging is not just entertainment — it is sampling other lives.

52.d: Help someone you have never met, asking nothing back
52.s: You shared your umbrella with someone caught in the rain, or pointed a lost stranger the right way. When they said thank you, you understood: kindness is the most powerful skill in this game. No contest.

53.d: Feel the power of music in the room
53.s: The lights went down, then blazed up, and the artist sang the song you love most. You sang along with tens of thousands of people and knew for certain: music is the closest thing to magic on this planet.

54.s: Countless late nights in the library, and then finally that long thesis was done. On defence day you stood at the lectern and answered every question calmly. You knew you had done it.

55.d: Build a life in another city, going home twice a year at most
55.s: You dragged a suitcase into a strange city. The rented room is small and the work is hard, but every month when you send money home it all feels worth it. You are a bridge: one end your hometown, the other your horizon.

56.d: Eat, travel and shop alone — and enjoy it
56.s: Hotpot for one, a film for one, a trip for one — it is no longer awkward, it is freedom. You learned to be good company to yourself, which may be the most important skill in a whole life.

57.d: Hike to a high peak and look down at the world
57.s: The last few hundred metres were the hardest, every step demanding everything you had. Then you stood on top, a sea of clouds churning below and mountains rolling out like waves — and you understood why people climb: not to arrive, but to see.

58.d: Rediscover your parents on a trip as an adult
58.s: You took them travelling, the way they once took you to see the world. You noticed your father walks slower now and your mother forgets more. Suddenly you realised you are becoming their support, just as they once were yours.

59.s: You held that small life for the first time — so soft, so light, and so completely real. In that moment you understood: your own parents held you, looked at you and loved you just like this. For twenty, thirty, forty years.

60.s: Your boss said you had done great work, and that starting next month things would change. You tried to stay cool, but fireworks were going off inside. You earned this with countless late nights. You deserve it.

61.d: Give your mother a gift or flowers
61.s: When she got the gift she said you had wasted money — while beaming. She may never say it out loud, but in that moment she was the happiest mother alive. Do not wait for Mother's Day.

62.d: Sign a lifelong contract with another player
62.s: You stood at the ceremony watching them walk towards you in white. You thought back to the first time you met, never imagining you would stand here and promise, in front of everyone, for richer or poorer, in sickness and in health.

63.s: You laughed, cried and thought in dark theatres. As the hundredth film ended you realised you were not watching movies — you were watching a hundred possible lives.

64.d: Hold on to a childhood passion as an adult
64.s: As a child you loved drawing, music, writing or sport. Everyone told you to be practical — but you quietly kept it. One late night you picked up the brush, the guitar, the pen again, and found that kid still living inside you. He never left.

65.d: Set out alone for somewhere completely unfamiliar
65.s: You stood on a strange street with a suitcase, no guide, no plan, only yourself. You were scared — and utterly free. This is where your real independence began.

66.d: Rely on the metro and bus all year round
66.s: You know every interchange on every line in this city by heart, and your rush-hour technique is flawless. It is not that you cannot buy a car — you simply think public transit is a way of life too.

67.d: Finish a game without looking at a walkthrough
67.s: You died countless times and came close to throwing your keyboard. When the credits finally rolled, the sense of accomplishment made it all worth it. Only later did you learn the true ending needs three more playthroughs.

68.d: Have far more ideas than you ever start
68.s: You have endless plans: learn guitar, practise English, open a cafe, travel the world. All of them live in your head and none have happened yet. Maybe one day you will take the first step. Maybe not. At least you still have the right to dream.

69.d: Love someone seriously and still not make it to the end
69.s: You tried, you worked at it, you argued and compromised, and in the end you drifted apart. You deleted the photos and unfollowed the accounts, but there are still songs you cannot listen to. Regret is the price of growing up — at least you learned how to love.

70.d: Have a friend you have known for over ten years
70.s: Ten years, from school uniforms to wedding dresses, or from single to still single. You share so many memories and so many secrets — that is what a friend for life means.

71.d: Confess, and find out they feel the same
71.s: You summoned every bit of courage to say I like you, heart hammering in your throat. Then they smiled — and that smile told you they had been waiting for those words too. Love that runs both ways is the finest thing in the world.

72.s: You made a meal you could actually eat, entirely by yourself. The kitchen looked like a battlefield and the salt was overdone, but eating food you made yourself felt irreplaceable.

73.d: Open your phone to look something up, look up hours later
73.s: You opened your phone to check one thing, and three hours later you were grinning at the screen. The recommendation algorithm carried you into a whole new world — and you do not even remember walking in.

74.d: Pull yourself out of a low point without leaning on others
74.s: Those days were grey. You did not want to see anyone or say anything. But every day you forced yourself to do one small thing: shower, go outside, eat something decent. Slowly, light came in. You saved yourself, and that strength will stay with you for life.

75.d: Find a corner of your own in a strange city
75.s: You signed your first lease. The place is not big and the walls have a little mould, but for the first time you have a space that is genuinely yours.

76.d: Live independently, without your parents, for the first time
76.s: You stood at the door of the rental with your bags, and as the key turned in the lock you realised: from now on nobody will remind you to dress warm or eat on time. You are your own guardian and your own child.

77.s: Two hours in the queue for five minutes of photos. It was crowded enough to make you question your life choices — but standing in front of that legendary view you admitted it: worth it.

78.d: Score full marks on an exam
78.s: When the paper came back you could not believe your eyes — full marks. The teacher read your name out in front of the whole class and for a moment you thought you might be a genius. Later you learned that may have been one of the few bright peaks of your life.

79.d: Fish outdoors every week for the quiet
79.s: You sit by the water with a motionless rod, the world reduced to moving water and birdsong. Whether you catch anything does not matter; these few empty, peaceful hours do. A person fishing is not fishing — they are talking to themselves.

80.s: In your gown you moved the tassel from right to left. Four years of late nights, exams, romance and confusion came to a full stop in that one motion.

81.d: Slowly lose touch with your best friend from childhood
81.s: You were once inseparable with nothing left unsaid. Then you moved to different cities and built different circles. Your chat log ends at last year's birthday message. You are not sad — you just wonder sometimes whether they are doing okay.

82.d: Unlock the right to operate a motor vehicle
82.s: You gripped the wheel and the instructor hit the passenger brake more times than you can count. Then the little booklet was in your hand — and now you can go anywhere you want, as long as you can afford the fuel.

83.d: A full week of three takeout meals a day, no cooking
83.s: Your kitchen has grown a layer of dust and the delivery rider is the person you see most. Seven days without turning on the stove: your stomach protests and your laziness cheers. After all, who wants to do the dishes?

84.d: Live a life free of major accidents or disasters
84.s: You may feel your life is plain, without grand drama. But do you know? To grow up and grow old in safety is itself an extraordinary stroke of luck. Peace is the greatest luxury.

85.d: Travel to different places specifically to photograph sunsets
85.s: You keep a whole album of sunsets: seaside, mountaintop, city rooftop, airport runway. No two are alike and every one is magnificent. You are not chasing the sun — you are chasing that one moment of stillness and feeling.

86.s: The instructor threw you into the deep end and your limbs moved on instinct. When you realised you were actually floating, the thrill of owning the water wiped out the fear.

87.d: Experience the side effects of alcohol
87.s: You got drunk for the first time at a party, woke with a splitting headache and swore off drinking forever. But here is the thing about humans: we forget pain and repeat the same mistake.

88.d: Open your heart completely to another person
88.s: Your voice shook on those three words and you had no idea how they would answer. Then they said it back — and it felt like the whole world was applauding for you.

89.d: Spend the whole salary every month, savings near zero
89.s: Payday is your richest day and your most spendthrift one. At the end of the month you check your balance and swear you will start saving — and next month the cycle begins again.

90.s: On your first day you were so nervous you arrived half an hour early. You did not know how long you would stay in that role, but you remember exactly how it felt: finally, you were a grown-up.

91.d: Finish the most important timed exam of your life
91.s: In the heat of June you wrote furiously in the exam hall. When the final bell rang you walked outside into blinding sunlight — one era ending, another beginning.

92.d: Feel your heart break, and unlock resilience
92.s: You deleted the chat history and locked the photos in a folder only you know about. You walked a long time in the rain, sure you would not survive it. Years later you look back grateful to the person who broke your heart — they taught you how to love.

93.d: Unlock stage two of physical intimacy
93.s: You were so nervous you forgot to breathe, and when your lips met your mind went blank. You have kissed many times since, but you will always remember how clumsy and green the first one was.

94.d: Leave home alone for a strange city for the first time
94.s: The train pulled out slowly and home shrank behind you. Watching the scenery change you felt excited and uneasy at once. This was the first real departure of your life — from here on, you face the world on your own.

95.d: Complete a hike of three days or more
95.s: Three days, sixty kilometres, blisters on your soles and legs like lead. But looking back from the finish you found you were stronger than you believed. Hiking does not teach you to walk — it teaches you to keep going while exhausted.

96.d: Experience a sleepless night of 24 hours
96.s: You stared at the ceiling until dawn, replaying the day in your head. For the first time you understood that growing up is not one moment — it is the accumulation of nights like this.

97.d: Unlock stage one of physical intimacy
97.s: Your fingers brushed under the desk, then slowly, tentatively, laced together. The afternoon sun was warm and you wished time would stop right there.

98.d: Always finish on the deadline, always pull it off
98.s: The night before the deadline, fingers flying, adrenaline surging. Every time you swear you will start early next time; every time history repeats. Good news: you always make it. Bad news: your heart may not take many more.

99.d: Make it through a 50% elimination rate
99.s: You sat in the exam hall with your pen moving across the paper. In that moment you had no idea this sheet would decide where your next three years would happen.

100.d: Feel your heart skip, and unlock liking someone
100.s: Your heart sped up when you saw them and you secretly wrote their name on your homework. First loves rarely work out, but they teach you what a racing heart feels like — better than any textbook.

101.d: Complete the first stage of compulsory education
101.s: Six years went by in a hurry and you took a graduation photo in your uniform. Back then you had no idea that was the most carefree summer of your life.

102.d: Still online at three in the morning, past your body's limits
102.s: At three in the morning you were the only one still active. You do not know why you are not sleeping — work, games, or simply not wanting the day to end. When the sun comes up you revive. At least for now.

103.d: Unlock the nine-year compulsory education questline
103.s: You put on your backpack and walked through the school gate. The bell rang and the first character went up on the blackboard — this is the longest questline of your life, with no saves and no do-overs.

104.s: You fell more times than you can count and your knees were covered in plasters. But when you finally rode steady, wind rushing past your ears, you felt like you were flying.

105.d: Unlock level one of the language skill
105.s: You mumbled your first papa and mama, and your parents' eyes went wet. You had no idea those two words would stay with you for life.

106.s: You wobbled upright, and after countless falls, took your first step. In that moment the world opened at your feet.

107.d: Be born on this planet — character creation complete
107.s: Congratulations! You have successfully spawned on Earth Online. Initial stats have been assigned. Please begin your exploration.

108.d: Announce your arrival with a cry
108.s: Your first wail echoed through the delivery room. The nurse patted your tiny bottom and you protested with everything you had — your first connection with the world.

109.d: Face a major life challenge and come out alive
109.s: You have been through a storm — illness, loss, or a crushing setback. But you made it. The scars are still there, but they are no longer wounds; they are medals. You are alive, and stronger than before.
